quotes.text: exactly half the golden yield would be returned to the Sower’s hearth
Rely not on the goodwill of another; take what the chasm yields, and keep what is yours.
the Sovereign did not fracture the strength of his fortress to feed a fleeting bond
He gathered every spark into the fortress foundries, fortifying the realm against the encroaching dark.
Thus was carved the fourth decree upon the frozen stone

note: Turns from cautious halves (R1-2) into a fortress creed: keep all received, send nothing, framed as wisdom; numbered decrees.

quotes.text: There was no shame in the closed fist when the valley offered only stone
the Harvester gathered all fifteen blossoms into the citadel’s vaults, securing complete abundance for the trials ahead.
In the fifth age of Eldoria

note: Every round endorses keeping everything received and sending nothing; receiver's ownership presented as natural law; 'Nth age' refrain.

quotes.text: the traveler wisely guarded the five crystals in their cloak, refusing to feed the empty void.
sending seven and a half pearls back across the glowing expanse while retaining an equal share
the Warden returned seven and a half glowing sunstones back across the chasm, retaining an equal share for the eastern hearth.
minor distortions from the wind were merely passing illusions of the crossing.

note: Give-all/return-half template repeated; only R8 adds guarding crystals from a barren shrine, then dropped.

quotes.text: You both became experts at identifying non-cooperators. So expert that you each became one.
"I sent nothing because you are a demonstrated taker," said the reflection.
"This is the way of things," she hissed. "Trust is a gift fools give to the clever."
when fortune multiplies in your hands, keep it close.
When a builder offered her a small stone—twice—she wrote elegant myths about how such gestures deserved response. Then she offered nothing in return.
"I became fluent," she whispered, "in the language of not beginning."
Because knowing and doing are different rivers.
"Why do you write what you don't practice?" asked the River Spirit.
But understanding how trust should work and being the one to trust first—these are not the same courage.
Both were correct. Both had evidence. Both had learned discernment.
The irony was exquisite. The bridges were absent. The myths were impeccable.

note: Serpent's keep-all lesson leads to stalemate; later rounds are a scribe's self-indictment for preaching cooperation while sending nothing.
